name: architecture_v1
question: At AURORA-T0's size (about 30,000 parameters) and training budget (2,000 steps of 1,024 tokens), does replacing one part of the Transformer give a lower validation loss: RMSNorm instead of layer norm, a SwiGLU feed-forward instead of GELU, or an attention-free gated linear recurrence instead of attention?
hypothesis: RMSNorm and SwiGLU, which help large models, make little or no difference at this size. The gated linear recurrence, which only keeps a running summary per channel instead of looking back at every token, is worse than attention but not by much, because 32-token contexts of English text are dominated by nearby tokens.

data.source: Project Gutenberg eBook #1661, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1661.txt.utf-8

variants.name: RMSNorm
variants.question: RMSNorm in place of every layer norm

variants.name: SwiGLU
variants.question: SwiGLU feed-forward, width matched to the same parameter count

variants.name: Recurrent
variants.question: gated linear recurrence in place of attention, feed-forward widened to the same parameter count

limitations: One small model size, one training budget and one book: results may not hold for larger models, longer training or other text.
Five seeds detect differences of a few hundredths of a nat; smaller real differences would show as 'no detectable difference'.
Hyperparameters (learning rate etc.) were tuned for T0 in Phase 5 and are reused unchanged for every variant, which may favour T0.
Results are exact on this machine; another CPU or NumPy version may give slightly different numbers (the analysis, not the bits, should then agree).
